back: Days 1–3. Bright red. Blood + decidua + small clots. Moderate flow; never >1 pad / hour.
Days 4–10. Pink to brown. Serum + leucocytes + cervical mucus. Reversion to rubra = red flag.
Day 10 to 6 weeks. Whitish-yellow. Leucocytes + epithelial cells + mucus. Fresh red bleeding = late PPH / subinvolution.
Puerperal endometritis. Rx: cultures → IV clindamycin + gentamicin (WHO/ACOG).
Fundus fails to descend 1 cm/day. Persistent or reverted rubra past Day 4–5. Escalate to obstetrician.
Immediately postpartum fundus at umbilicus → descends ~1 cm/day → non-palpable by day 10 → pre-pregnancy size by 6 weeks.
≤6 pads / 24 h normal. Saturating ≥1 pad/hour = abnormal — assess for PPH.
May indicate retained clot / endometrial blockage. Encourage ambulation, bladder emptying; escalate if persistent with fundal enlargement.

front: Discharge teaching — alba returning to rubra
back: Return to bright-red bleeding after alba has started = subinvolution. Call provider immediately — do not wait for 6-week check.
